{{Short description|German chemist}}
'''Inke Siewert''' (born 5 May 1980) is a professor for Inorganic Chemistry at [[University of Göttingen]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Öffentlichkeitsarbeit|first=Georg-August-Universität Göttingen-|title=Inke Siewert – Georg-August-Universität Göttingen|url=https://www.uni-goettingen.de/en/inke+siewert/617920.html|access-date=2020-06-25|website=www.uni-goettingen.de|language=de}}</ref> Her research focuses on activation of small molecules by [[transition metal]] complexes and molecular electrochemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Öffentlichkeitsarbeit|first=Georg-August-Universität Göttingen-|title=Research – Georg-August-Universität Göttingen|url=https://www.uni-goettingen.de/en/research/617913.html|access-date=2020-06-25|website=www.uni-goettingen.de|language=de}}</ref>

== Education and professional life ==
She finished her [[Abitur]] in 1999.<ref name=":0" /> She then studied chemistry at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] from 1999 to 2004.<ref name=":0" /> From 2004 to 2009 she worked on her doctorate in the group of [[Christian Limberg]] at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]].<ref name=":0" /> The topic of her dissertation was "Activation of dioxygen at novel first row transition metal complexes for biomimetic oxidation reactions".<ref name=":0" /> From 2009 to 2010, she was a postdoctoral research fellow at the [[University of Oxford]] in the group of Simon Aldridge.<ref name=":0" /> From 2011 to 2013, she was a research fellow at the [[University of Göttingen]] in the group of Franc Meyer.<ref name=":0" /> From 2013 to 2016, she was an [[Emmy Noether]] group leader at the same university.<ref name=":0" /> Since 2017, she is a professor in Inorganic Chemistry at the [[University of Göttingen]].<ref name=":0" />
